name: @lovinka/vitrinka-mcp

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List all projects in the vitrinka artifacts library (name, branch count, set count, last update).

tools.name: list_sets
tools.description: List the artifact sets of a project (all branches) or of one branch — newest first, without file lists. Each set has a share URL, version, key, optional custom name and title.

branch.description: Branch slug; omit for all branches of the project

tools.name: get_set
tools.description: Get one artifact set: metadata (version, key, name, title, commit, PR, issue) plus its full file list and share URL.

selector.description: Set selector: a version number ("2"), "latest", the set's custom name, or its key

tools.name: rename_set
tools.description: Set (or change) the custom URL-addressable name of a set — e.g. name fixit/main v2 "payout-flow" so https://…/fixit/main/payout-flow resolves. Pass an empty name to clear it. Requires VITRINKA_TOKEN.

selector.description: Set selector: a version number ("2"), "latest", the set's custom name, or its key

name.description: New name: lowercase slug [a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}, not purely numeric, not "latest". Empty string clears the name.

tools.name: update_set
tools.description: Edit a set's mutable metadata: custom name and/or human title. Omitted fields stay untouched; empty string clears. Requires VITRINKA_TOKEN.

selector.description: Set selector: a version number ("2"), "latest", the set's custom name, or its key

name.description: New name slug; "" clears; omit to leave unchanged

title.description: New human title (max 200 chars); "" clears; omit to leave unchanged

tools.name: list_boards
tools.description: List the annotation boards (Freeform-style canvases over screenshot sets). Each has a slug, title and URL.

tools.name: scrape_board
tools.description: Read a WHOLE board as one structured testing digest — every media image (URL), note text and annotation — with the connect-tool edges walked into ordered journey chains ("flow": [[A,B,C]]). Use this to process a testing session end-to-end (pasted screenshots + notes) rather than acting on one annotation at a time; the flow tells you the user's step order. Images are absolute URLs (no auth on the mesh) — fetch them to SEE each step.

tools.name: wait_for_work
tools.description: BLOCK until annotation work exists — the continuous-work tool (board-v3). Long-polls the server: costs nothing while idle, returns up to 3 ready-to-act markdown capsules the instant the user annotates (or re-queues). {"idle":true} means the window elapsed quietly — simply call it again. A listening session (/vitrinka:listen) loops on this forever.

board.description: Only wait for one board's work (slug); omit for any board

tools.name: get_capsule
tools.description: One annotation's compact markdown work brief (same shape wait_for_work delivers): ask, region, source set, thread tail, protocol. Cheaper than get_annotation when you just need to act.

tools.name: list_work
tools.description: List annotation work items (the agent queue), FIFO. Each item: id, board, intent (fix|investigate|refactor|redesign|other), prompt, source set ref + file, crop URL. Filter by status (open = waiting for an agent) and/or board slug. Start here.

status.description: Filter by lifecycle status; use "open" to find waiting work

tools.name: get_annotation
tools.description: Get one annotation's full brief: region, intent, prompt revisions, thread messages (incl. file attachments the user added — fetch their URLs), fix attempts (before/after history), the element context (elements: E-numbers the region overlaps + screen siblings) and its card's source set. Fetch the cropUrl (PNG, no auth on the mesh) to SEE the annotated region — user markup strokes are baked in.

tools.name: set_status
tools.description: Move an annotation through its lifecycle. Agents use: "working" when picking an item up, "in_review" after attaching the after-shot and replying. Never "resolved" — the user accepts in the board UI. A 409 "cancelled" means the user withdrew the annotation mid-flight: revert your changes for it and move on. Requires VITRINKA_TOKEN.

tools.name: reply
tools.description: Post a reply into an annotation's thread as the agent (author "claude"). Use it to report what was done, ask a clarifying question, or explain a push-back. Requires VITRINKA_TOKEN.

tools.name: attach_after
tools.description: Attach the "after" proof shot to an annotation: names a file inside a set version you already pushed (vitrinka snap/push). Appends a fix attempt to the before/after deck AND advances the annotated card's face on the board immediately (the user's accept blesses it, reject rolls it back) — this is the canonical way to show a fix; never paste the after as a new card. Requires VITRINKA_TOKEN.

selector.description: Set selector: a version number ("2"), "latest", the set's custom name, or its key

file.description: File path inside that set, e.g. "2026-07-04/01-domov.png"

tools.name: highlight
tools.description: Visually highlight a rectangle on an annotation's shot card — draws an ink rectangle on the board that appears live for the user (SSE). Defaults to the annotation's own region; pass x/y/w/h (source-image pixels) to point at something else on the same card, e.g. "the element you actually mean is HERE". Requires VITRINKA_TOKEN.

id.description: Annotation id — the highlight lands on its card

color.description: CSS color; default #ffb020 (agent amber, distinct from the user's red ink)

instructions: Vitrinka is BOARD-FIRST: the annotation board is the default surface for sharing and reviewing UI work. When publishing screenshots/journeys, create or update the flow board (cli.ts board-from-set) and hand the user the /boards/<slug> URL as the primary link; set/share pages are the archive behind it. Boards are live and interactive: the user annotates regions and thread replies route to claude by default (@eve only when explicitly mentioned) — a session in the app repo keeps listening via /vitrinka:listen, which arms a native background monitor (`vitrinka watch`) that re-invokes the session on each new annotation (zero-token idle); the session then drains the queue via wait_for_work.
